title: Expunge automation with attestation checksum and customer timeline
creator: Maya Thompson
description: Deliver an automated expunge pipeline that ties retention TTLs to per-tenant policies, emits verifiable deletion attestations (signed checksums), and produces a customer-facing timeline artifact for Right-To-Be-Forgotten requests. The goal is to make deletion actions auditable, reproducible across hosted/dedicated/private modes, and consumable by customer compliance teams and auditors.
acceptance_criteria: A policy authoring surface exists for per-tenant TTLs and selective retention exceptions (UI + config API)
Scheduled expunge job enqueues and runs across shards without impacting live inference (measured by <5% tail latency increase during runs)
For each deleted record group, the system emits an attestation bundle: signed checksum, region stamp, model/version tags, and deletion timestamps
Customer-facing timeline artifact generated on RTBF completion: includes request id, impacted resource types, attestation reference, and cryptographic proof link
Attestations are retained in an append-only ledger and searchable by request id for 90 days by default
End-to-end tests + a sample GH action/Playbook demonstrating verification against the attestation ledger
notes: We avoid full synchronous deletion in the request path; RTBF requests enqueue a coordination workflow to schedule phased expunge to minimize application impact.
Attestation format proposal: SHA-256 over canonicalized record ids + deletion metadata, signed by Redwood KMS key (customer-specific signing optional for Private).
For Dedicated/Private customers, provide an option to store attestations in customer-managed S3 or HSM-backed vaults.
We need to coordinate with Runtime team to ensure KV cache eviction and expunge idempotency across replicas.
Investigate alignment with existing deletion-proof formats used in legal/compliance teams; avoid reinventing cryptographic formats.
Estimate assumes use of existing job-scheduler infra and the console will host the timeline artifact viewer.
